title: Prove hard-link identity and deletion semantics
goal: Identify shared inode content and metadata, then remove an extra name without losing the remaining file.
challenge: Create a hard link to a small original, prove device/inode/link-count identity, demonstrate shared edits and permissions, remove one name and verify the remaining contents. Preserve an independent before-copy.

steps.command: w=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/local-hardlinks.XXXXXX") && cd "$w" && pwd && here() { case "$w" in "$HOME"/local-hardlinks.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; test "${w%/*}" = "$HOME" && test -d "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && test "$(realpath -e "$w")" = "$w" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a "$w")" = learner:700 && test "$(pwd -P)" = "$w"; }; fresh() { for f; do test ! -e "$f" && test ! -L "$f" || return 19; done; }; here
steps.explanation: Create a unique learner-owned guest workspace; stop on error and record its absolute path. Reopening boots the disk, not these shell variables. Never use the host terminal.
steps.expected: A new private directory; no pre-existing files are changed.

steps.command: here && fresh original.txt before.txt alias.txt && { printf 'known\n' > original.txt; chmod 0640 original.txt; cp -p original.txt before.txt; ln -- original.txt alias.txt; }
steps.explanation: A hard link is a second directory entry for the same inode; before.txt is an independent copy. No directory or cross-filesystem hard linking is attempted.
steps.expected: Two names share one inode; independent before-copy.

steps.command: here && { stat -c '%d:%i %h %a %n' original.txt alias.txt before.txt; cmp original.txt alias.txt; }
steps.explanation: Equal bytes alone are insufficient: compare device plus inode and link count.
steps.expected: original and alias have identical device/inode and link count 2; before differs.

steps.command: here && { printf 'added\n' >> alias.txt; chmod 0600 alias.txt; cat original.txt; stat -c '%a' original.txt; cat before.txt; }
steps.explanation: Writes and chmod act on the shared inode. This intentionally changes the teaching original; the independent before-copy retains its earlier state.
steps.expected: Both names show known plus added and mode 600; before remains known.

steps.command: here && { rm -- alias.txt; stat -c "%h" original.txt; cat original.txt; cmp -s before.txt original.txt; printf "comparison status=%s\n" "$?"; }
steps.explanation: Unlink one name, not an independently copied file. The data remains reachable through original.txt.
steps.expected: Link count 1; modified data survives; before differs.

hints: Preserve an independent copy before deliberate shared edits.
review: I retained actual output and checked the required contents, metadata or identity, not just command success.
I can explain the stated limitations, demonstrate the incorrect case, preserve originals and clean up only my recorded workspace.
